message.content:
**Hydrogen – Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **Physical State (STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (at 0 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (121.5 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.0 K) |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (Cp) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (Cv) | 20.786 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Enthalpy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard molar entropy | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Standard molar Gibbs free energy | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| **Chemical Properties** | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | –0.754 eV |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride) |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Reactivity | Highly flammable; reacts with O₂, N₂, halogens, acids, etc. |
| | Acid–base behavior | Acts as a weak acid (HF) or base (H⁻) depending on context |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Forms H‑bond in water, alcohols, etc. |
| | Solubility in water | ~1.6 g L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| | Solubility in organic solvents | Very soluble in non‑polar solvents (e.g., hexane) |
| **Isotopic Variants** | Protium (¹H) | Most abundant (~99.98 %) |
| | Deuterium (²H) | Stable isotope; used in NMR, heavy water |
| | Tritium (³H) | Radioactive; β‑emitter (half‑life ≈12.32 y) |
| **Applications** | Fuel | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Analytical | Used as a tracer, in mass spectrometry |
| | Medical | MRI contrast agents (deuterated compounds) |
| | Energy | Potential clean energy carrier |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe.
- **Diatomic gas**: At room temperature and pressure, it exists as H₂ molecules.
- **Highly reactive**: It readily forms bonds with many elements, especially oxygen and nitrogen.
- **Key role in life**: Integral part of water (H₂O) and organic molecules.
- **Fuel potential**: Clean combustion produces only water; central to hydrogen‑fuel cell technology.

Feel free to ask if you’d like deeper details on any specific property or application!
